E1.label: previous set P (may be empty), next set N

E2.label: compute P ∩ N — cards spotlit in both lines

E3.label: those spotlights DO NOT MOVE — they stay lit on their card

E4.label: leftover lights L = P minus N; leftover targets T = N minus P

E6.label: pair L to T — chart E2 assignment

E7.label: pair as many as possible; surplus lights RETIRE (chart E3)

E8.label: pair as many as possible; surplus targets get NEW spotlights (chart E4)

E9.label: each paired light TWEENS its circle centre from old card to new card over travel_fraction, easing

E10.label: its beam re-aims every frame: origin fixed, wide end tracks the circle

E11.label: arrival: every travelling light within epsilon of its target

F1.label: leftover lights L, leftover targets T

F3.label: sort both by target x; pair in order. Provably minimises beam crossings

F4.label: greedy nearest: each light takes its closest free target

G3.label: no glow, no circle, no beam. The dim still darkens it

G6.label: GLOW: the card's own light shader, ON AT ALL TIMES, over the whole card, at glow_strength

G7.label: is the focus highlight also on this card?

G8.label: BOTH read distinctly — glow is a coloured bloom, highlight is the existing modulate 1.825 brightening

G11.label: glow at full, no circle, no beam, no dim

G12.label: the light layer draws OVER the whole board: dim everywhere, minus the circle and beam holes

G13.label: so the glow on a spotlit card reads ONLY inside its circle or beam; outside, the dim cancels it and it looks unlit

G14.label: a card that is spotlit but has NO light instance (e.g. naturally spotlit, elsewhere on the board) is dimmed like everything else, so its glow vanishes — Q127=a. That is what makes the beam MEAN something

H2.label: input: dim level d (0..1), and for each live spotlight: circle centre, circle radius, origin point, beam width at each end, per-light intensity

H4.label: for each spotlight: add its BEAM contribution (a cone, narrow at the origin, widening to fully contain the circle)

H5.label: for each spotlight: add its CIRCLE contribution (brighter than the beam — owner)

H6.label: coverage ACCUMULATES, so two beams crossing are brighter than one — the stacked-alpha effect the brief asks for

H8.label: final additive light = clamp(coverage) * light colour

I1.label: the first beam of a spotlight rises — QR2=d, this is also what raises the dim

I2.label: initial origin count k0 = the size of the first section's set, minimum 4 (Q109=a) — so the common case is perfectly even

I3.label: place k0 origins evenly across the origin BAND — even in x, and each with a deterministic y scatter of a few lamp-heights, because no two origins may share a y even when their targets share a row (Q113=d, Q250=a)

I5.label: a new spotlight needs an origin

I7.label: take the one NEAREST its target (Q111=a) — keeps beams mostly vertical and mostly non-crossing

I8.label: SUBDIVIDE: every midpoint between adjacent existing origins becomes a candidate

I9.label: pick candidates at random until the request is satisfied; the rest join the pool

I10.label: is this origin above the viewport?

I11.label: PINNED — it does not move while it is on screen (Q164)

I12.label: x RE-SPREADS every frame to fill the visible width (Q251=b, Q262=a). Invisible, so moving it costs nothing to look at; it is pinned again the moment it comes back into view

J2.label: MODEL 1 — REJECTED. Screen-anchored. Origin line = viewport top, always. Beams never leave the screen; length is bounded by the viewport. Scrolling slides the CIRCLES but the origins stay put, so beam angles change as you scroll

J3.label: MODEL 2 — ✅ CHOSEN, as (d) with two refinements: x re-spreads while the origin is off the top, and no two origins share a y. When a spotlight is created, its origin is pinned in BOARD space at (allocated x, target card y minus origin_rise). It scrolls with the board: scroll down and origin+circle+beam all slide up off screen together and new ones rise from below. Beam angle is constant. Length is bounded by origin_rise

J4.label: MODEL 3 — REJECTED. Hybrid. Origin is placed at the viewport top AT CREATION TIME, then converted to board space and pinned there. Reads screen-anchored while still, content-anchored while scrolling

K1.label: spotlight set for this line is known

K2.label: for each spotlit card, walk its COLUMN upward: every card at a HIGHER z in that column is covering it

K3.label: the row that must expand is the spotlit card's OWN row z: growing the gap below row z pushes rows z+1.. down

K4.label: is the spotlit card already the last card of its column?

K5.label: already fully visible — no expansion needed for it

K6.label: mark row z as a reveal row

K7.label: apply the expansion to EVERY column, or only to columns that actually have a card at row z?

K8.label: rows stay straight across the board; short columns simply have nothing to push

K9.label: the board goes ragged: row z+1 sits at different heights in different columns

K10.label: the reveal row's control height grows, tweened — by the DERIVED amount at K10b, never to a fixed full card height

K10b.label: ⚠ v6 — HOW FAR IT OPENS IS DERIVED (supersedes Q43=a). The covering cards duck by exactly enough that there is NO VISIBLE GAP between the top of a ducking card and the top of a lifted card, sized from the LOWEST lifted card in that row. Where a row holds a card that did not lift, a gap is allowed there

K10c.label: ⚠ AND THE DUCK IS COMPUTED ONCE, NOT LIVE-TRACKED. Worked out from the geometry at the moment the duck begins; once finished it stops tracking card bottoms, so a card moving afterwards may open a gap under it and that is accepted

K10d.label: 🔶 FOR REVIEW — under Q265=c only the MELD lifts, but the reveal exists to uncover a buried LIT card, and a lit non-meld card never lifts. Is the opening sized by the lifting cards, the lit cards, or the larger of the two?

K11.label: cards below ease down to their new anchors — CardVisual.delta_self_moving_logic already smooths this for free

K12.label: the ROW SCORE GUTTER labels for that row must grow identically or the score numbers desync from their rows

K13.label: PlayArea.slot_center_global must account for the expansion or every prop anchored to a row below it lands in the wrong place

K14.label: the scroll content grows taller; see chart H for what that does to the view

L4.label: score_line returns immediately at D2 for every remaining line

L6.label: NEW: the light layer must be torn down and every row collapsed HERE, because no further score_line will run

L7.label: pending_action = on_run_scorer is persisted; resume replays the whole submit from the pre-act board

L8.label: NEW: the dim phase replays from scratch. Origins are re-allocated, so the beams will NOT be in the same places as before the quit

L9.label: the spotlit card may no longer be where the light is pointing

L10.label: NEW: lights re-pin to their card's live position every frame, so a card that moves drags its light with it

L11.label: a card that leaves the board entirely: its light retires (chart E3)

L12.label: card_scale / card_separation_scale change relayouts the whole board. Reveal heights and light positions are all derived live, so they follow

L13.label: _resolve_game raises the win/lose overlay, which has its OWN dim ColorRect

L14.label: NEW: two dims must not stack into a black screen — the spotlight dim is fully down before the outcome overlay appears (C15 precedes C17)

R1.label: on_active handler discards a card at column c, row z, during line L

R2.label: the card leaves the board: zone_col.datas.erase — every card at higher z shifts down one index

R3.label: was the discarded card the LAST of its column?

R4.label: nothing was covering it, so nothing slides in. The card now at z-1 becomes topmost and NATURALLY spotlit — but it is in row z-1, so it is NOT part of this section. Q199=a — the light retires rather than following downward

R5.label: the card that was at z+1 is now at z: it occupies the discarded card's slot AND its row

R6.label: ⚠ THE SCORE MOVES. Q22=b re-evaluates the meld after every spotlight effect has fired (Q23=a, once), so the discarded card does NOT still score and the hand may be a different hand — C2

R7.label: the discarded card's JUMP is skipped: its visual is gone by D14

R8.label: its light does NOT retire, and Q200=c means it does not MOVE either: the light is pinned to the SLOT, and the replacement card arrives underneath it. Nothing has to travel

R9.label: the new occupant joins the line's spotlight set and is force-spotlit

R10.label: skill_active_check runs — it already runs after every mod call, §1.1 — and fires on_active on the new occupant

R11.label: that handler discards a card too?

R12.label: re-enter at R1. A cap is needed or a column can unzip itself in one line. Q201=b — NO per-section cap: only the act-level runaway guard bounds it

R13.label: the line continues at D13, the hold beat, with the original meld and a changed board

R14.label: every card BELOW the discard in that column also moved up one row. Q202=a — and note the direction: compaction pulls cards UP, into the section being scored now or into ones still pending, so nothing is skipped there. Only a discard in a row the cascade already PASSED moves cards into scored rows

R15.label: the reveal rows were computed at D4 against the OLD indices. Q203=a — they are RE-DERIVED and re-tweened; the board settles into its new shape mid-section rather than holding a stale gap

R16.label: the column is one card shorter, so the board is shorter: every reveal below it, every prop anchored below it, and the scroll extent all move — chart I, K13

M10.label: a card with StampRevealing sits covered

M11.label: it is spotlit, so it glows — through the top ~45 px strip that shows. Q142=a: exactly the case a player needs to be told about

M12.label: a card with StampGlobal sits in the draw deck

M13.label: it is spotlit anywhere. Does it glow in the deck viewer? Q143

M15.label: is_active() true when their column is empty — and Q141=b says YES, they glow, same rule everywhere. No header special case

M17.label: always spotlit, only visible in the rules viewer — and Q144=a says NO glow: every rules card is always active, so a uniformly glowing list says nothing

T1.label: any board mutation: a card placed, a stack dropped by Next, a card gaining an ability mid-game, resume, act start

T2.label: skill_active_check() runs — it already runs after every mod call and at game start

T3.label: did this card transition from not-spotlit to spotlit?

T4.label: nothing. A card that was already spotlit is not re-cued (Q13, Q15)

T5.label: does it have anything to announce? Q246=a — it must have a SKILL that implements on_active; anything else has nothing to show

T6.label: MOMENTARY SPOTLIGHT: a circle and a beam spawn on it, hold, and retire

T7.label: glow only — there is nothing to show happening

T8.label: its glow fades in and STAYS — the glow is the persistent state, the spotlight is the announcement — chart F

T10.label: the dim rises with this spotlight's BEAM and falls when it retires — during ORDINARY PLAY, not only during a submit. Q245=c: a SHALLOWER dim outside scoring than inside it

T11.label: how many cards transitioned at once? Q247=a — one dim covering all of them, one cue, the lights spawn together and retire together

T13.label: N spotlights, ONE dim that covers all of them and falls when the last retires

T14.label: ✅ Q248=b — THIS CASE DOES NOT ARISE, and no code prevents it. CardModifierSkill.active is @export_storage: a card saved active LOADS active, so there is no transition and no cue. A card saved inactive that loads uncovered transitions normally, as in play

T15.label: does it block input while it plays? Q249=a — NO. It is a flourish; a second cue may start while the first is still retiring

T16.label: the player keeps playing; a second cue can start while the first is still retiring

T17.label: REJECTED — a short lockout per cue, which on a Next that drops four stacks would be four lockouts in a row

N2.label: hosts a REAL board: real PlayArea, real CardVisuals, real light layer, real styles

N3.label: a SCENARIO selector — one entry per usage listed in §15

N4.label: a play/step control: run the scenario at real pacing, or step it one phase at a time

N5.label: a viewport-size control, so origin spread can be judged at every aspect ratio

N6.label: every tunable from §16 live in the inspector, re-read while the scenario runs (the fx_editor polls, because a custom resource does not announce its own edits)

N7.label: freeze control — hold the whole thing on one frame to judge a silhouette

O1.label: glow quad: host body plus reach, one per host — same sizing as fire, FxRequest.reach

O2.label: body_near early-out: reject the empty corners of the quad before any lookup — worth 2.1x on fire

O3.label: p = fx_local(UV, extent, pixel) — quantized on the HOST'S ORIGIN, never rotated

O5.label: d = signed distance from p to the mask, measured against the host's EXACT deformed outline — Q124=b, the 24-vertex mask the fire shader already carries. Not a rounded rect

O6.label: d = length(p - centre) - circle_radius. One subtraction. This is why the circle is the CHEAP client

O7.label: falloff(d): mix of a smooth curve and inverse-square, per the braindump. Inverse-square is what makes the core read HOT instead of foggy

O8.label: how many layers? Q207 — between 2 and 4, and it is a KNOB: owner picks by eye rather than the design fixing it

O10.label: intensity = sum over layers of falloff(d / radius_i) * gain_i, the multi-exposure simulation — each layer its own reach and gain

O11.label: radial COLOUR SHIFT: core to mid to edge. This is a PaletteRamp SAMPLE on intensity, exactly as fire samples u_ramp — the palette contract forbids lerping colours, and a ramp is the fix, not a limit

O12.label: is this fragment OVER the host's own art?

O13.label: outside the silhouette: the halo. Draws at full alpha — this is the part that hangs off the card's edge

O14.label: over the art: draws at inner_alpha — the lever fire ships at the opaque end and this effect exists to use. Q216=d: START LOW (~0.35) and tune it by eye against scenario S15, the circle over a real card face

O15.label: ⚠ the over-art test is done at the UNQUANTIZED position, so the art's own edge slices the chunky glow pixels instead of a staircase — fire paid for this lesson twice, for cards and again for props

O16.label: dither on the FX PIXEL GRID (never FRAGCOORD) to break the ramp's bands

O17.label: COLOR = ramp sample * brightness * fx_intensity, alpha * opacity * inner_alpha

O18.label: multiply the host's MODULATE back in — or the focus highlight never reaches the glow, which is exactly Q121's problem

O18b.label: ⚠ Q121=b — the FOCUS HIGHLIGHT is being changed too, so that glow and highlight read distinctly on the same card. Not a glow-side fix alone

O19.label: blend mode — Q218: (c) additive OUTSIDE the card, tinted OVER the art, PROVIDED that produces no visible seam between the two. If it does, tint everywhere. Never blow out to white

O20.label: light adds. Bright, correct for a lamp, and harmless out here because there is no art under it

O21.label: light tints. Keeps the card's contrast and cannot blow out — which is what keeps the rank glyph readable. ⚠ If the join between O20 and O21 shows a seam, tint BOTH

P1.label: the Dangerous Light pipeline, as written

P2.label: does this stage read the RENDERED SCENE?

P3.label: MULTI-LAYER GLOW — layers of radius and gain, summed. Doable inside the glow quad today: chart O, O10

P4.label: INVERSE-SQUARE FALLOFF — a function of one distance. Doable today: chart O, O7

P5.label: RADIAL COLOUR SHIFT core to mid to edge. Doable today, and it IS a PaletteRamp: chart O, O11

P6.label: GRAIN — a hash per pixel. Doable in the quad, but only over the quad, not over the frame

P7.label: HALATION — blur the BRIGHT parts of the scene, tint red, add back

P8.label: BLOOM — threshold the scene, wide blur, tint cyan, add back

P9.label: FILM LUT — a colour transform of every pixel in the frame

P10.label: CHROMATIC ABERRATION — resample the scene per channel

P11.label: GATE WEAVE — jitter the whole frame's sample point

P13.label: HDR TONEMAP — needs a float target to tonemap FROM

P14.label: ALL of these need a screen read. The project has ZERO today — §1.6 fact 1

P15.label: so they are one new subsystem: a full-screen pass over the whole game

P16.label: and it changes the look of EVERYTHING, not of the spotlight — QR10=a, IN SCOPE

P17.label: CHOSEN. A game-wide art-direction change, shipped as a SECOND deliverable AFTER Spotlight (Q239=a). Q230=c: on only while a dim is up. Q231=c: a LUT built from palette entries so the frame stays on-palette. Q232=b: bloom only, no halation. Q233=a: grain, dust and weave quantized to the game pixel. Q234=b: NO chromatic aberration. Q235=a: a real HDR viewport

P18.label: REJECTED — Spotlight would ship only the four stages that need no screen read

P19.label: REJECTED — the palette and the pixel grid would stay the only colour authorities
